target: route "realisation-space": R(s;S) as a semialgebraic realisation space, the inradius/bit-cost correspondence, the pinned shape and the level theorem, and the no-doubling barrier with B^3 as test case

findings.defect: The proof of the headline ("no doubly pinned game realises B^3 = B(B^2) of height 22 for ANY pin, any readouts and any block") silently identifies the BLOCK's pinned pair with the blow-up's outer pair (alpha_2,beta_2). The route's own definition of DOUBLY PINNED only requires the block to be a pinned extension at SOME pair of its Max vertices, and rs:no-outer-translate is explicitly scoped to "pinned extension with outer pair (alpha,beta)". GAP, in one sentence: it is not proved that a pinned extension whose pinned pair is a pair of coordinates other than the blow-up's outer pair cannot present B^2(.xor z) at its pinned drive. The same unjustified identification is made for the outer game (rs:level is applied as if G's pinned pair were the blow-up's outer pair).
findings.evidence: Exact enumeration (holes.py/holes2.py/holes3.py/holes4.py, my own code, cube combinatorics only). Doubling requires h_{B^2}(4 xor z)=10, i.e. z in {8,10,24,26} (verified: heights of B^2 = [4,2,4,3,0,1,2,3,6,5,8,2,10,8,10,2,5,7,3,9,4,3,4,9,6,7,8,9,10,8,10,9], sink 4, maxima 12,14,28,30). For the pair (alpha_2,beta_2)=(3,4) my code reproduces the route's numbers EXACTLY (z=8: |E_a|=8,|E_b|=5, 4 violations, including beta_2 at 2->1 and 4->3; z=16: 3; z=24: 7). But for z=26 (u=30, a legitimate maximal-height seed of B(B^2)) and the pinned pair {alpha_1,beta_2}={1,4}, on the face {sigma_1=sigma_4=0}={0,1,4,5,8,9,12,13} one gets E_alpha={0,1,5,8,9,13}, E_beta={1,5,8,9,12,13}, face BA steps 0->9,1->5,4->9,8->9,9->5,12->9,13->5 (face sink 5), and ZERO up-closedness violations for either set; an extra necessary condition I derived (at the layers (0,1),(1,1) the block values coincide, so alpha's switchability must be opposite there) also holds. So the stated obstruction does not fire. PARTIAL REPAIR, which the route does not give: applying rs:upclosed also at the outer game's OTHER layers, where the block must present the untranslated B^2, kills every one of the 4 doubling vectors and all 20 ordered coordinate pairs (holes4.py: 0 survivors; e.g. z=26,(1,4) has 2+2 violations against B^2). That repair is valid only when the block's pin rows do not read the outer drive, since otherwise (Theta_u,Theta_w) move with the drive and the monotonicity argument fails. As it stands the headline is unproved, and so is the derived cap of 16.

findings.defect: The hypotheses are insufficient for the conclusion, and the proof step "(C3),(C4) by the assumption on Phi" is invalid. The hypothesis controls only Phi = R_alpha - A R_beta - q_A, but (C4) demands Psi = R_beta - A' R_alpha - q_B > 0 exactly when phi = 0, and this does not follow. Secondary defect: the hypothesis mentions A and q_A, which are only chosen inside the proof (A=A'=3/4, q_A a multiple of 2^{-D''}), so the hypothesis is not well formed.
findings.evidence: With A=A'=3/4, q_B=0: Phi<0 <=> b > (4/3)(a-q_A); Psi>0 <=> b > (3/4)a; and (4/3)(a-q_A) < (3/4)a exactly when a < (16/7)q_A = Theta_u, which the corollary's own setting guarantees. So Phi<0 is STRICTLY WEAKER than Psi>0 and cannot imply it. Explicit family satisfying every stated hypothesis with the conclusion's construction failing: take R_beta = 0 (substochastic, values below t_1, so (C2) holds), R_alpha any substochastic readout with R_alpha - q_A of the sign of phi (so the Phi hypothesis holds); then Psi = -(3/4)R_alpha < 0 at every strategy, so at any phi=0 strategy beta is not switchable at the layer (1,0) although B_phi(s,z) demands it. The phi=1 half is fine (Phi>0 and b<Theta_w give Psi<0). The corollary is repaired by adding the symmetric hypothesis on Psi.

findings.result_name: rs:metric (The open question of rem:blowup-realise is a metric one)
findings.defect: The stated equivalence is false in one direction. From rs:inradius one has c <= log2(1/rho)+2 and log2(1/rho) <= (n+2)c + log2(6(n+1)); with n = O(k) these give c=O(k) => log2(1/rho)=O(k^2), but log2(1/rho)=O(k^2) only gives c = O(k^2), i.e. denominators 2^{O(k^2)}, NOT the additive regime 2^{O(k)}.
findings.evidence: Direct: c <= ceil(log2(1/rho))+1; substituting log2(1/rho) = O(k^2) yields c = O(k^2). No inequality in rs:inradius upgrades that to O(k). The second clause of rs:metric (poly(k) vertices iff log2(1/rho) = poly(k)) IS correct, because poly is closed under multiplication by n+2. The route's headline ("rem:blowup-realise's additive regime is EXACTLY a metric statement") rests on the false clause; the true statement is an equivalence up to the factor n+2, i.e. only at the poly/superpoly grain.

findings.defect: The claim "the drive line [0,1] has exactly 16 interior breakpoints and 17 cells of constant outmap" does not reproduce. The exact partition into maximal intervals of constant OUTMAP has 13 interior breakpoints and 14 cells. 16/17 is the common refinement of the outmap partition with the tau-optimality partition (3 further points at which the optimal Min strategy changes without changing the outmap) - a different object from the one rs:drive(e) and rs:b2-window(a) name.
findings.evidence: drive.py/drive2.py, exact Fractions, block {c1,c2,c3,c6} of prop:b2-realised driven by y_{c5}: 14 cells with fences 0, 47723619/255897160, ..., 1: outmaps (0,1,3,6,7,4,5,2)[=B^1], (0,1,3,6,5,4,7,2), (0,1,3,2,5,4,7,6), (1,0,3,2,5,4,7,6), (5,0,3,2,1,4,7,6), (5,4,3,2,1,0,7,6), (5,4,7,2,1,0,3,6), (5,4,7,2,0,1,3,6), (7,4,5,2,0,1,3,6)[=translate], (7,4,5,6,0,1,3,2), (7,6,5,4,0,1,3,2), (7,6,5,4,0,1,2,3), (7,6,4,5,0,1,2,3), (7,6,4,5,0,3,2,1). Interior outmap breakpoints: 13. Interior points where some optimal-tau set changes: 3. Union: 16, hence 17 cells of constant (outmap, optimal tau). Everything else in rs:b2-window reproduces EXACTLY: B^1 on [0,47723619/255897160) (width 0.18649530537970802), the translate on (1175936917/2026652880, 10168377/16341335) (width 278278286482313/6623642728158960 = 0.04201287688710535), tau-optimality switches 0 or 1 per sigma, margin sign-change census 22 once / 2 twice (the two are (sigma=3,c3) and (sigma=7,c3)), Theta_w = 2036/3313 inside the window at distances 0.03432 and 0.00770.

findings.defect: The reported "smallest outer margin 16281932731/53967650046976 = 3.0170e-4" for prop:b3-outer is not a margin: it is min |Psi| = min |R_beta - A' R_alpha - q_B|. The smallest improvement margin of that game is 200226176318423/56589182615657906176 = 3.5382e-6, 85 times smaller. The same phrase in the same sentence DOES denote the improvement margin for prop:b2-realised (1447620941/889411092480, which I confirm is the minimum over all 5*32 incidences), so two different quantities are reported under one name. This matters because mu = smallest margin is the input of rs:inradius's certified lower bound on the robustness.
findings.evidence: b3b.py/b3c.py, exact. After correcting the target order to the paper's (x,a1,b1,a2,b2,a3,b3,c_min,t1) my reconstruction of prop:b3-outer reproduces the paper exactly (outmap = B_{p,0}(B^2), no ties, USO, acyclic, height 12, run 44,83,45,81,40,80,32,71,33,69,36,68,4; Theta_u=2048/4093, Theta_w=2046/4093; (C1)-(C4) hold at all 128 strategies with no exception; largest off-layer drive 26928313173661/53967650046976 < Theta_w, exactly as claimed). The candidate quantities are: min|a-Theta_u| = 260868159322/215712491838157 = 1.2093e-3; min|b-Theta_w| = 9.0645e-4; min|Phi| = 3.0553e-4; min|Psi| = 16281932731/53967650046976 = 3.0170e-4 (the route's number); min|margin at alpha_3| = 4.7205e-6; min|margin at beta_3| = min over all incidences = 3.5382e-6.

findings.defect: "(C1) and (C2) force y_beta^L(sigma) < Theta_w for every L != (0,0) and every sigma" is asserted but does not follow: (C1) is imposed only at the layers (0,0),(1,0) and (C2) only at (0,0),(0,1), so neither bounds the drive b at the layer (1,1). The conclusion is nevertheless TRUE, by lem:layer-order plus lem:switch (from (1,1,v) an outer edge leads to (1,0,v) or (0,1,v) and thence to (0,0,v); the step that switches beta raises val(beta) strictly), which is not the argument given.
findings.evidence: Counterexample to the implication as stated: A=A'=3/4, q_A=1/10, q_B=0 (Theta_u=0.16, Theta_w=0.12); at the layer (1,1) take a=0.5, b=0.9: (C3) with phi=0 needs a < Ab+q_A = 0.775 (true) and (C4) with phi=0 needs b > A'a = 0.375 (true), yet b = 0.9 > Theta_w. The clause is used again in rs:where(ii) to order the four drives, so the repair is needed there too.

findings.defect: "Twenty-three FURTHER dyadic pins (A,A',q_A) of denominator 512 with q_B=0 realise B^2" is wrong twice: (i) the published pin (502,509,8) is itself in the list of 23, so at most 22 are further; (ii) 5 of the 23 have A+q_A = 512, i.e. an action row with ZERO leak, so they are not points of P_S^{>0} and hence not points of R(s;S) as the route's own def:rs-def-space requires. Inside R(s;S) the count is 18 total, 17 further.
findings.evidence: pscan.py/pscan2-4.py (float prefilter over all 512^3 pins via the necessary condition Theta_w = A'q_A/(1-AA') in the exact translation window) followed by pexact.py (exact Fraction verification of every survivor). All 23 realise B^2 exactly with no tie: (496,511,10),(498,511,9),(499,510,9),(500,509,9),(500,511,8),(501,508,9),(501,510,8),(501,511,7),(502,507,9),(502,509,8)*,(502,510,7),(503,506,9)+,(503,508,8),(503,509,7),(503,511,6),(504,507,8)+,(504,508,7),(504,510,6),(505,507,7)+,(505,509,6),(506,508,6)+,(508,511,3),(509,510,3)+ ; * = the published pin, + = zero-leak row (min leak 0).

findings.defect: The three pins said to have been built into games are named (500,511,8),(502,509,8),(496,511,10), but (502,509,8) IS the published pin of prop:b2-realised and the third built game in the route's own directory is B2_pin_500_509_9.json, i.e. the pin (500,509,9). The vertex counts 137/138/139 are correct once the list is corrected.
findings.evidence: gver.py/gver2.py, my own verifier, from the game files: B2_small_GAME.json 138 vertices (136 non-sink, 5 max, 1 min, 130 avg); B2_pin_500_511_8.json 137; B2_pin_496_511_10.json 138; B2_pin_500_509_9.json 139. All four: greatest trap empty, 0 tied incidences, outmap = B^2 (values taken as the componentwise minimum over both Min strategies, exact rational elimination), USO, acyclic, height 10, run 12,19,13,17,8,16,0,7,1,5,4, value vector nondecreasing along the run.

findings.defect: "The exact axis-parallel upper bound rho <= 1633/2^23 = 1.9467e-4, attained by raising the t_1-entry of c_5's action-0 row" is not exact: the exact threshold in that coordinate is 416874941/2141891461120 = 1.9462934e-4 < 1633/2^23 = 1.9466877e-4 (the stated number is the smallest multiple of 2^-23 ABOVE the threshold). Three further slips in the same sentence: (a) the perturbed coordinate is 0 in the published normal form, so it is a coordinate of P_S only if the shape S contains t_1 in that row, and the shape S is never specified anywhere in the route although rho(theta) depends on it; (b) the axis-parallel number bounds rho(theta) for the published point, not rho(s;S) = sup_theta rho(theta), which is the quantity in rs:inradius's inequalities; (c) "a bit cost of 9" is an upper bound c(s;S) <= 9, not a computed minimum.
findings.evidence: axis.py: the margins are affine in that coordinate for each (sigma,tau), so the exact first sign change is a rational root; the smallest positive one is 416874941/2141891461120, and the outmap is B^2 just below and not just above. axis3.py: an exact scan of all 84 shape coordinates in both directions, discarding perturbations that leave P_S, breaks at no direction for eps = 1.946e-4 and only at (c5, action 0, t_1) for eps = 1.9463e-4, so the direction identified is right. The certified lower bound reproduces exactly: mu*delta/(6(n+1)) = (1447620941/889411092480)(1/256)/42 = 1447620941/9562948066344960 = 1.5138e-7, min leak = 1/256 attained at (c3,1),(c4,0),(c6,1).

findings.defect: "Each L_S(X) is a relatively open polyhedron" is false as soon as k >= 1: at a Min vertex the constraint is X_sigma(u) = min_a(p^{u,a}.X_sigma + q^{u,a}), a disjunction (one branch tight, the other slack), so the fibre is a union of at most 2^{k 2^m} relatively open polyhedra, not one. The fibration and the disjointness are unaffected.
findings.evidence: min(L_0,L_1) = c is equivalent to (L_0=c and L_1>=c) or (L_1=c and L_0>=c); each branch is linear in theta but their union is not convex. The route itself files (d) as a restatement of the paragraph after thm:readout-realise, where the programme is set up with the Min actions fixed.

findings.defect: Sign error in the proof: "the margin of (sigma,x_j) in theta^{(j)} is minus that of (sigma xor e_j,x_j) in theta" is wrong - it is EQUAL to it. With the stated sign the j-edge would come out reversed relative to s^{e_j} and the conclusion would fail; with equality the conclusion is exactly s^{e_j}.
findings.evidence: Delta'_{x_j,sigma} = F'_{x_j,1-sigma_j}(val'_sigma) - val'_sigma(x_j) = F_{x_j,sigma_j}(val_{sigma xor e_j}) - val_{sigma xor e_j}(x_j) = Delta_{x_j,sigma xor e_j}, since (sigma xor e_j)_j = 1-sigma_j. The STATEMENT verifies: swap.py exchanges the two rows of each of c_1..c_5 of prop:b2-realised in turn and the outmap is B^2(. xor e_j) in all five cases, with no tie.

findings.defect: "the shape of prop:b2-realised and prop:b3-outer, the only shape in which a level of the tower has been realised" is inaccurate: prop:b2-realised is NOT doubly pinned. Its inner block {c_1,c_2,c_3,c_6} contains no pinned pair (c_2's action 0 reads only c_3 with 509/512, but c_3's action 0 reads c_6 and t_1, not c_2; c_1's action 0 reads three targets). Only prop:b3-outer is doubly pinned. So the barrier's class excludes the shape in which the second level actually was realised, which narrows it further than the route says.
findings.evidence: Read off the printed normal form of prop:b2-realised; a pinned pair requires two Max vertices whose action-0 rows form a closed two-cycle A y_beta + q_A, A' y_alpha + q_B, and no pair among {c_1,c_2,c_3} does.

findings.defect: The height identity h(S)+2+h_S(o_S xor z) is cited from prop:blowup-height, which states it for B(s,z) with the PARITY readout; here it is used for B_phi with an arbitrary readout phi. The inequality actually needed (height <= h_S+2+h_S(o_S xor z) for every phi) is true - off the layer (0,0) each bottom-antipodal step drops the inner height by exactly one, at the inner sink the outer square is a USO of the 2-cube with sink (0,0) so at most two further steps, and the layer (0,0) contributes h_S(o_S xor z) - but it is not what the cited proposition says. Separately, the cap 16 bounds only blow-ups: a pinned extension's outmap need not be of blow-up form at all (its layer-(0,0) outer part is an arbitrary up-closed pair of sets, not necessarily empty).
findings.evidence: prop:blowup-height, last sentence: "The four formulas hold for B(s,z) with an arbitrary z" - arbitrary z, not arbitrary phi; its proof reads the parity in the layer dynamics. Cap input verified: max over purely inner z of h_{B^2}(4 xor z) = 4 (at z = e_beta1), so 10+2+4 = 16.

findings.result_name: rs:inradius (det bound) and rs:def-space (vertex count citation)
findings.defect: Two asserted steps. (i) "|det M| <= 2^{nD}" needs det(I-P) <= 1 for a substochastic nonnegative P, i.e. Ostrowski's inequality det A <= prod a_ii for nonsingular M-matrices - an unproved import; the bound survives via Hadamard at the cost of an additive (n/2)log2 n in rs:inradius. Also "margins have denominator dividing 2^{(n+1)D}" is false as written (det M need not be a power of two); the correct statement is denominator dividing 2^D det M <= 2^{(n+1)D}, which gives the same bound mu >= 2^{-(n+1)D}. (ii) rs:def-space cites thm:readout-realise(b) for "m Max, k Min and O(n^2 D) average vertices", but that theorem spends 2m(r-1) Min vertices on a readout system; the k-Min claim follows from lem:dyadic-row's consequence (|C|+2+O(|C|^2 d) vertices), which the definition also cites. Minor bookkeeping: the outer conditions of rs:level number 2*4*2^m, not 4*2^m; rs:cost's vertex count should read O((m+2+k)^2 D'').
findings.evidence: Cramer plus the M-matrix property give everything else in rs:inradius correctly; I checked the perturbation chain (row leak >= delta/2, ||(I-P')^{-1}||_inf <= 2/delta, ||x-x'||_inf <= 2(n+1)eps/delta, |Delta-Delta'| <= 5(n+1)eps/delta, eps < mu delta/(6(n+1))) and it is sound as written.

findings.defect: The route returns "new-barrier". By the paper's own convention this is not a barrier in the sense of sec:gap: like prop:tstar and thm:deformed-flat it closes a construction avenue and covers none of M1-M6 or def:bsi. Those two results say so explicitly in their statements; rs:no-doubling does not.
findings.evidence: prop:tstar: "Like thm:deformed-flat, this closes a construction avenue and is not a barrier in the sense of sec:gap: it constrains one rule for building orientations and covers none of the mechanisms M1-M6 or def:bsi." No step of the route assumes a target-equivalent oracle, and no decision rule is claimed, so THE STANDING RULE (rem:own-successor, the Z_0/Z_1 seed, vacuous stalls) does not bear on it.

verdict: NOT SOUND: five major defects, one of them in the headline. What I rebuilt from the statements in exact rational arithmetic, and what reproduces EXACTLY: prop:b2-realised's normal form (outmap B^2, no ties, USO, acyclic, height 10, sink 4, run from 12, min leak 1/256, min margin 1447620941/889411092480); its pinned structure (Theta_u=2048/3313, Theta_w=2036/3313, pinned-layer values constant, (C1)-(C4) with no exception at all 32 strategies, largest off-layer drive 270545851903/778234705920 < Theta_w); prop:b3-outer's normal form (after correcting the target order to the paper's) with outmap B_{p,0}(B^2), height 12, the exact run, Theta_u=2048/4093, Theta_w=2046/4093, (C1)-(C4) with no exception at all 128 strategies, largest off-layer drive 26928313173661/53967650046976 < Theta_w; the two drive-line windows and their exact fences and widths, the tau-switch bound and the 22/2 margin sign-change census; B^2's heights, maximal vertices 12,14,28,30 and the doubling vectors {8,10,24,26}; the up-closedness violation counts 4/3/7 and E=empty for the two realised targets; B_p(B^2,8) as an acyclic USO of the 7-cube of height 22 with the stated 22-step walk; the certified robustness lower bound 1447620941/9562948066344960; four games verified FROM THE GAME (138/137/138/139 vertices, empty trap, no tie, outmap, USO, acyclicity, height, run, monotone values); rs:where(iii)'s drive-plane witness (all three windows exact) and the c_3-perturbation fences 0.5885/0.6151/0.6418; rs:swap on all five coordinates. rs:semialg and rs:inradius are, modulo two asserted linear-algebra steps and the polyhedron slip in (d), correct as proved. What fails: (1) rs:no-doubling's proof identifies the block's pinned pair with the blow-up's outer pair although \"doubly pinned\" does not - for the doubling vector z=26 and the pinned pair {alpha_1,beta_2} the obstruction does not fire (|E_alpha|=|E_beta|=6, zero violations), so the headline \"for any pin\" is unproved; a repair exists (apply the same lemma at the outer game's untranslated layers - 0 of 80 configurations survive) but it is not in the route and is valid only when the block's pin rows do not read the outer drive. (2) rs:cost's hypotheses control Phi but not Psi, and (C4) does not follow (explicit failing readouts R_beta = 0). (3) rs:metric's \"iff\" is false in the \"if\" direction. (4) rs:b2-window(a)'s 16 breakpoints/17 cells is the refinement with the tau-optimality partition; cells of constant OUTMAP number 14 (13 interior breakpoints). (5) the b3 \"smallest outer margin\" 3.0170e-4 is min|Psi|; the actual smallest margin is 3.5382e-6. The route's own \"gap\" and \"shape-specific\" caveats are honest, but the barrier is narrower still than stated: prop:b2-realised is not doubly pinned, so the class does not even contain the shape in which the second level was realised.
